title: Describing changes over time / Nwere ebe ike n'ulo oru
bridge: Na Igbo, mgbakwunye ndoro ndoro na-egosi na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali. Na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali. Na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali. Na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali. Na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali.
rule: Iji egosi ndoro ndoro na Igbo: 1) Jiri 'nwe' + okpukpere (ma ọ bụ nkume) iji egosi ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro ndoro: 'nwe ike', 'nwe mma', 'nwe ike'. 2) Jiri 'banye' + okpukpere/azumahia iji egosi ndoro ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro ndoro: 'banye onye nkuzi', 'banye nke'. 3) Jiri 'tinye' + azumahia ma ọ bụ okpukpere iji egosi ndoro ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro ndoro: 'tinye ahụ', 'tinye nke'. 4) Iji egosi ndoro ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro ndoro, ọ dịghị na 'nwe' ma ọ bụ 'banye' na-akpali na-akpali. 5) Na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali. 6) Na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali. 7) Na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali na-akpali.

concept_examples.translation: Ndị mmadụ nwere ike n'ulo oru.

concept_examples.text: The city has changed a lot.
concept_examples.translation: Ulo a nwere ike n'ulo oru.

concept_examples.text: She became more confident after the course.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ ya nwere ike n'ulo oru n'oge a.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃi bɪˈkeɪm mɔːr ˈkɑːnfɪdənt ˈæftər ðə kɔːrs/

concept_examples.text: The leaves turn yellow in autumn.
concept_examples.translation: Azụmahia nwere ike n'ulo oru n'oge uguru.

common_error.wrong: I am more tired now than before.
common_error.correct: I have gotten more tired now.
common_error.correct_alt: I have become more tired now.
common_error.explanation: N'ime Igbo, ọ bụrụ na ị na-akpali na 'mụ nwere ike n'ulo oru' iji egosi ndoro ndoro. Ma na Igbo, 'mụ nwere ike' na-egosi ndoro ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro ndoro. Iji egosi ndoro ndoro, ị ga-eme ka 'nwe' ma ọ bụ 'banye' (ma ọ bụ 'nwere' ma ọ bụ 'banye'). ọ bụrụ na ị na-akpali na 'mụ nwere ike n'ulo oru', ị ga-eme ka 'mụ nwere ike n'ulo oru'.

examples.original: It is getting colder.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈɡetɪŋ ˈkoʊldər/
examples.translation: Ọ nwere ike n'ulo oru (ọ nwere ike n'ulo oru).
examples.note: Jiri 'nwe' + nkume iji egosi ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro ndoro. Na Igbo, ọ bụrụ na ị na-akpali na 'nwere ike n'ulo oru', ị ga-eme ka 'nwere ike n'ulo oru'.

examples.original: My English is getting better.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz ˈɡetɪŋ ˈbɛtər/
examples.translation: Akwụkwọ m nwere ike n'ulo oru (ọ nwere ike n'ulo oru).
examples.note: Ebe a, 'nwe ike' nwere ike n'ulo oru na Igbo. ọ bụrụ na ị na-akpali na 'nwere ike n'ulo oru', ị ga-eme ka 'nwere ike n'ulo oru'.

examples.original: The days are getting longer.
examples.phonetic: /ðə deɪz ɑːr ˈɡetɪŋ ˈlɔːŋɡər/
examples.translation: Ubochi nwere ike n'ulo oru (ọ nwere ike n'ulo oru).
examples.note: Ọ bụrụ na ị na-akpali na 'nwere ike n'ulo oru', ị ga-eme ka 'nwere ike n'ulo oru'.

examples.original: He became famous after the video.
examples.phonetic: /hi bɪˈkeɪm ˈfeɪməs ˈæftər ðə ˈvɪdi.oʊ/
examples.translation: Ọ banye nke n'oge a.
examples.note: Para cambios de estatus (famoso, rico) se prefiere 'become'. En español se dice 'hacerse'.

examples.original: The situation became complicated.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən bɪˈkeɪm ˈkɑːmplɪkeɪtɪd/
examples.translation: Ndoro ndoro nwere ike n'ulo oru.
examples.note: Aquí 'become complicated' equivale a 'volverse complicado'.

examples.original: She became a doctor in 2010.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi bɪˈkeɪm ə ˈdɑːktər ɪn tuː ˈθaʊzənd ˈtɛn/
examples.translation: Ọ banye onye nkuzi n'oge a.
examples.note: Con profesiones o roles, se usa 'become' + sustantivo sin artículo.

levels.label: Expressing changes with used to and no longer
levels.translation: Iji 'nwere' ma ọ bụ 'banye' na-akpali na-akpali

examples.original: I used to live in Madrid.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ juːst tʊ lɪv ɪn məˈdrɪd/
examples.translation: Mụ nwere ike n'ulo oru n'oge a.
examples.note: Para describir hábitos o estados pasados que ya no son ciertos, se usa 'used to' + verbo base.

examples.original: I no longer eat meat.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ noʊ ˈlɔːŋɡər iːt miːt/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ị na-akpali na 'mụ nwere ike n'ulo oru', ị ga-eme ka 'nwere ike n'ulo oru'.
examples.note: En español se usa 'ya no', en inglés 'no longer' es más formal que 'don't... anymore'.

examples.original: She didn't use to smoke, but now she does.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi ˈdɪdnt juːst tʊ smoʊk bʌt naʊ ʃi dʌz/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ị na-akpali na 'mụ nwere ike n'ulo oru', ị ga-eme ka 'nwere ike n'ulo oru'.
examples.note: En negativo se usa 'didn't use to' (sin -d final en 'use'). Cuidado con la pronunciación: /juːst/.

title: Speculating and making deductions / Especular na emume nke ọma / emume nke ọma na ndoro ndoro
bridge: N'igbo anyị na-eme ka 'ọ bụrụ na' ma ọ bụ 'ọ nwere ike ịbụ' iji emume nke ọma. N'ụkwụ anyị na-eme ka 'must', 'might', 'could', 'can't' + infinitive. Nke a bụ, 'must' na-egosi emume nke ọma pụtara (positive) ma 'can't' na-egosi emume nke ọma pụtara (negative); 'might', 'may' na 'could' na-egosi ike ịbụ. Chọpụta: adịghị ịkpọ 'must not' iji emume nke ọma n'ụkwụ, n'ihi na 'must not' n'ụkwụ na-egosi ihe ọ bụla nwere ike ịbụ ihe ọ bụla n'ụzọ ọma.
rule: Iji emume nke ọma n'oge ugbu a n'ụkwụ anyị na-eme ka modals ndị a na-akpọ na ndị a na-akpọ na ndị a na-akpọ na ndị a na-akpọ: 'must' (emume nke ọma pụtara na ihe niile dị ịchara), 'can't' (emume nke ọma pụtara na ihe niile adịghị ịchara), 'might', 'may', 'could' (ike ịbụ, ndoro ndoro). Iji emume nke ọma n'oge gara aga, anyị na-eme ka 'must have + participle', 'can't have + participle', 'might have + participle', etc. Nke a bụ: subject + modal + verb base (preset) ma ọ bụ modal + have + participle (past). Nkwado: n'igbo, 'ọ bụrụ na' na 'adịghị ịbụ' dị ịchara, mana n'ụkwụ anyị adịghị na-akpọ 'must not be' iji emume nke ọma n'ụzọ ọ bụla; anyị na-eme ka 'can't be'.

concept_examples.text: He must be tired after the long trip.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ nwere ike ịdị mma n'oge ndoro ndoro gara aga.
concept_examples.phonetic: /hiː mʌst biː ˈtaɪərd ˈæftər ðə lɔːŋ trɪp/

concept_examples.text: She can't be serious about moving to another country.
concept_examples.translation: Adịghị ịbụ na ọ na-eme ka ọ nwere ike ịbụ n'ụzọ ọma.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː kænt biː ˈsɪriəs əˈbaʊt ˈmuːvɪŋ tuː əˈnʌðər ˈkʌntri/

concept_examples.text: They might have forgotten the meeting.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ nwere ike ịbụ ha jiri nweta ụbọchị ndoro ndoro.

concept_examples.text: It could rain later, so take an umbrella.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ nwere ike ịzụọ n'oge ndoro ndoro, n'ihi na ọ nwere ike ịzụọ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt kʊd reɪn ˈleɪtər soʊ teɪk ən ʌmˈbrelə/

common_error.wrong: He must not be at home because the lights are off.
common_error.correct: He can't be at home because the lights are off.
common_error.correct_alt: He must be out because the lights are off.
common_error.explanation: N'error a na-eme n'ihi na n'igbo anyị na-akpọ 'adịghị ịbụ' iji emume nke ọma negative, mana n'ụkwụ anyị, 'must not' na-egosi ihe ọ bụla nwere ike ịbụ ihe ọ bụla n'ụzọ ọma ('adịghị ịbụ' = adịghị nwere ike ịbụ). Iji emume nke ọma n'ụzọ ọma, anyị na-eme ka 'can't' (ma ọ bụ 'couldn't' iji nwere ike ịbụ n'ụzọ ọma). Alternative 'must be out' dị ịchara n'ihi na nke a bụ emume nke ọma pụtara na ọ adịghị n'ụlọ.

examples.original: You're a journalist. You must meet a lot of people.
examples.phonetic: /jʊər ə ˈdʒɜːrnəlɪst. juː mʌst miːt ə lɒt əv ˈpiːpl/
examples.translation: I bụ journalist. Ọ bụrụ na ị nwere ike ịmụ maka ndị ọtụtụ.
examples.note: Anyị na-eme ka 'must' mgbe anyị nwere ike ịmụ maka ihe dị ịchara n'ụzọ ọma. N'igbo, 'ọ bụrụ na'.

examples.original: That can't be the right answer.
examples.phonetic: /ðæt kænt biː ðə raɪt ˈænsər/
examples.translation: Ọ adịghị ịbụ nke a bụ nkọmà nke ọma.
examples.note: Anyị na-eme ka 'can't' iji kwuo na ihe niile adịghị ịbụ. N'igbo, 'adịghị ịbụ'.

examples.original: He must have a lot of money because he drives a Ferrari.
examples.phonetic: /hiː mʌst hæv ə lɒt əv ˈmʌni bɪˈkɒz hiː draɪvz ə fəˈrɑːri/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ nwere ike ị nwere ego dị ukwuu n'ihi na ọ na-egwu Ferrari.
examples.note: N'ihi na ụzọ a na-akpọ 'because' (n'ihi na) na-egosi emume nke ọma.

levels.label: Possibility with might, may, and could

examples.original: She might be at the gym right now.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː maɪt biː æt ðə dʒɪm raɪt naʊ/
examples.translation: Ọ nwere ike ị bụ n'ụlọ ọrụ a na-aga ugbu a.
examples.note: 'Might' na-egosi ike ịbụ ndoro ndoro karịa 'must'. N'igbo, 'ọ nwere ike ịbụ'.

examples.original: They may arrive late because of the traffic.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ meɪ əˈraɪv leɪt bɪˈkɒz əv ðə ˈtræfɪk/
examples.translation: Ọ nwere ike ị ga-eri nke ọma n'ihi na ụgbọ ala adịghị ịdị mma.
examples.note: 'May' dị ịchara na 'might', mana ọ nwere ike ị bụ n'ụzọ ọma karịa. Ọ bụla dị ịchara.

examples.original: This could be the best restaurant in the city.
examples.phonetic: /ðɪs kʊd biː ðə best ˈrestərɒnt ɪn ðə ˈsɪti/
examples.translation: A nwere ike ị bụ nke a bụ nri ndoro ndoro n'ụlọ ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: 'Could' nwere ike ịbụ ike ịbụ na-akpọ n'ụzọ ọma n'okpuru ndoro ndoro.

levels.label: Deductions about the past
levels.translation: Emume nke ọma n'oge gara aga

examples.original: He must have studied a lot for the exam.
examples.phonetic: /hiː mʌst hæv ˈstʌdid ə lɒt fɔːr ði ɪɡˈzæm/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ nwere ike ị nweta ụbọchị ndoro ndoro n'oge gara aga.
examples.note: Anyị na-eme ka 'must have + participle' iji emume nke ọma n'oge gara aga. N'igbo, 'ọ bụrụ na ọ nwere ike ị nweta'.

examples.original: She can't have seen us because she didn't wave.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː kænt hæv siːn ʌs bɪˈkɒz ʃiː dɪdnt weɪv/
examples.translation: Adịghị ịbụ ha jiri lee anyị n'ihi na ha adịghị ịgba ike.
examples.note: 'Can't have + participle' na-egosi emume nke ọma negative n'oge gara aga. N'igbo, 'adịghị ịbụ ha jiri'.

examples.original: They might have missed the bus.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ maɪt hæv mɪst ðə bʌs/
examples.translation: Ọ nwere ike ị bụ ha jiri nweta ụbọchị.
examples.note: 'Might have + participle' na-egosi ike ịbụ n'oge gara aga. N'igbo, 'ọ nwere ike ị bụ ha jiri'.

examples.original: The roads are wet. It must have rained.
examples.phonetic: /ðə roʊdz ɑːr wet. ɪt mʌst hæv reɪnd/
examples.translation: Ụzọ ndoro ndoro adịghị ịdị mma. Ọ bụrụ na ụzọ ndoro ndoro adịghị ịdị mma.
examples.note: N'ihi na ndoro ndoro dị ịchara (ụzọ ndoro ndoro) anyị na-eme ka emume nke ọma pụtara n'oge gara aga.

translations.ig: Especular na emume nke ọma / emume nke ọma na ndoro ndoro

title: Expressing regret and hypothetical situations / Expresar arrepentimiento e hipótesis
bridge: Na Spanish, i na-eme ka ndị Igbo na-eme n'okpuru nke a na-akpọ 'condicional' na 'subjunctive' maka ịkpọta n'ime na ịkpọta n'okpuru (dịka 'if I had time, I would go'). Na English, nke a dịghị otú na Spanish: a na-eme ka nke a na-akpọ 'past simple' (ma ọ bụ 'past perfect') na clause 'if' na 'would' + verb na clause ndị na-akpọ 'main'. Ọ bụrụ na ndị Igbo na-akpọ n'okpuru 'if I would have', mana na English, clause 'if' adịghị na-eme ka 'would' dị. Mgbe ndị Igbo na-akpọ n'ime na ịkpọta n'okpuru, a na-eme ka nke a na-akpọ 'past perfect' ('had + participle') n'ime clause 'if' na 'would have + participle' na clause ndị na-akpọ 'main'.
rule: Na English B1, maka ịkpọta n'ime na ịkpọta n'okpuru (second conditional), i na-eme ka 'if + past simple' (ma ọ bụ 'if + past continuous') na clause 'if', na 'would + base form' na clause ndị na-akpọ 'main'. Examples: 'If I had more time, I would travel.' (Ọ bụrụ na m were ụzọ ụtọ, m ga-emela ugbu a). Jụọ na 'were' na-akpọ na ndị a na-akpọ 'if I were' (ọ bụrụ na 'was' na-akpọ na English informal). Maka ịkpọta arrepentimiento na okpuru (third conditional), i na-eme ka 'if + past perfect' (had + participle) na clause 'if' na 'would have + participle' na clause ndị na-akpọ 'main': 'If I had studied, I would have passed.' (Ọ bụrụ na m were nwere ike ịmụta, m ga-achọpụta). I nwere ike ịme ka 'I wish' + past perfect maka arrepentimiento: 'I wish I had studied.' (A chọrọ m inwere ike ịmụta). Jụọ na clause 'if' adịghị na-eme ka 'would' ma ọ bụ 'will'. Na ịkpọta ndị a, 'were' na-akpọ na-eme ka ọ dị mma: 'If he were here...'.

concept_examples.text: If I had more money, I would buy a car.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na m were ụzọ ụtọ, m ga-achọ ụgbọ ala.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ hæd mɔːr ˈmʌni aɪ wʊd baɪ ə kɑːr/

concept_examples.text: I wish I knew the answer.
concept_examples.translation: A chọrọ m inwere ike ịmụta.

concept_examples.text: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ were nwere ike ịmụta ndụmọdụ ndụ, ọ ga-achọpụta ụgọ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf ʃiː hæd ˈstʌdid ˈhɑːrdər ʃiː wʊd hæv pæst ði ɪɡˈzæm/

concept_examples.text: I would travel more if I were younger.
concept_examples.translation: M ga-emela ugbu a nwere m were ike.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd ˈtrævl mɔːr ɪf aɪ wɜːr ˈjʌŋɡər/

common_error.wrong: If I would have time, I would go to the party.
common_error.correct: If I had time, I would go to the party.
common_error.correct_alt: If I had time, I'd go to the party.
common_error.explanation: Ọ bụrụ na ndị Igbo na-akpọ 'if I would have time', mana na English, clause 'if' adịghị na-eme ka 'would'. Instead, we use past simple (had). I na-eme ka clause 'if' na-eme ka 'past simple' (ma ọ bụ 'past perfect') na clause ndị na-akpọ 'main', na 'would' na-eme ka ọ dị n'ime clause ndị na-akpọ 'main'.

levels.label: Second conditional (present/future hypotheticals)
levels.translation: Second conditional (ịkpọta n'ime na ịkpọta n'okpuru)

examples.original: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ wʌn ðə ˈlɑːtəri aɪ wʊd ˈtrævl ðə wɜːrld/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na m were ụzọ ụtọ, m ga-emela ugbu a.
examples.note: Jụọ na 'won' na-akpọ 'past simple', mana ọ adịghị na-eme ka 'won' n'ime a.

examples.original: If he were taller, he could play basketball.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf hiː wɜːr ˈtɔːlər hiː kʊd pleɪ ˈbæskɪtbɔːl/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na m were ndụ, m ga-eme ka m na-achọ ụzọ ụtọ ụkwụ.
examples.note: Na English formal, 'were' na-akpọ na ndị a na-akpọ 'if I were', mana 'was' na-akpọ na informal.

examples.original: What would you do if you had a million dollars?
examples.phonetic: /wʌt wʊd juː duː ɪf juː hæd ə ˈmɪljən ˈdɑːlərz/
examples.translation: Gịnị ka ị ga-eme ka ị were ụzọ ụtọ na ndụ?
examples.note: Ọ bụrụ na ndị Igbo na-akpọ n'ime clause 'if', mana na English, clause 'if' na-akpọ n'ime clause ndị na-akpọ 'main'.

examples.original: If I had known, I would have come earlier.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ hæd noʊn aɪ wʊd hæv kʌm ˈɜːrliər/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na m were nwere ike ịmụta, m ga-achọpụta ugbu a.
examples.note: Usa 'past perfect' (had + participle) na clause 'if' na 'would have + participle' na clause ndị na-akpọ 'main'.

examples.original: She wouldn't have missed the train if she had left home on time.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ˈwʊdnt hæv mɪst ðə treɪn ɪf ʃiː hæd left hoʊm ɒn taɪm/
examples.translation: Ọ adịghị ụzọ ụtọ ịzụ ụgbọ ọsọ nwere ike ịzụ ụgbọ ọsọ na nke a.
examples.note: Na English, 'would not' na-akpọ 'wouldn't'.

examples.original: If we had booked in advance, we would have got a discount.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf wiː hæd bʊkt ɪn ədˈvɑːns wiː wʊd hæv ɡɒt ə ˈdɪskaʊnt/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na anyị were nwere ike ịmụta n'oge mbụ, anyị ga-achọ ụgọ ndoro.
examples.note: En inglés británico 'got' se usa como participio; en americano a veces 'gotten'.

examples.original: I wish I had studied more for the test.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪʃ aɪ hæd ˈstʌdid mɔːr fər ðə test/
examples.translation: A chọrọ m inwere ike ịmụta ugbu a.
examples.note: Na 'wish' + past perfect, na-akpọ arrepentimiento na okpuru.

examples.original: I wish I could speak English fluently.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪʃ aɪ kʊd spiːk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈfluːəntli/
examples.translation: A chọrọ m inwere ike ịkpọta English nwere ike.
examples.note: Na 'could' + verb, na-akpọ ịkpọta n'ime na ndị a na-akpọ 'ability'.

examples.original: I wish it weren't raining today.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪʃ ɪt wɜːrnt ˈreɪnɪŋ təˈdeɪ/
examples.translation: A chọrọ m inwere ike ịdị na mmehie ugbu a.
examples.note: Na 'wish' + past continuous, na-akpọ ịkpọta n'ime na ndị a na-akpọ 'situation'.
